Treatment-emergent adverse effects, including myalgia and hepatic transaminase elevation, led to dose modification in 12% of participants, though discontinuation rates remained comparable between groups. These data highlight the importance of dual targeting lipid and inflammatory pathways to mitigate atherosclerotic progression in high-risk populations.

Exploratory metabolomic profiling identified branched-chain amino acid modulation as a potential mediator of metabolic benefits. These results support multifactorial targeting of enteroendocrine pathways for diabetes management while underscoring the need for long-term cardiovascular safety surveillance.
